what_would_wow_me: I would sign this. To be wowed I need five things. (1) Share company costs by work day or by hours worked, so a Monday to Friday week does not always beat the job margin and the month to date number does not drop on a Sunday. (2) Put one note on the month in progress in Month close so 21.5% there and 26.5% on Home do not look like a bug. verdict_paragraph: Round four fixed all six of my round three issues, and I proved each one by hand. The big one was the company number for part months. It now takes each month's company costs by the day, the screen says 'Company costs for 19 of 30 days', and the parts add back to the month to the cent in every split I tried. Month close did not move. Warehouse services with no cost now say 'No cost yet' in place of a 100% margin, on the screens, in the pivot and in the CSV. A day of work can no longer be deleted with one tap or overwritten by a second save, and stale edits are refused with the fresh day. Work cannot be dated after today. Home and month close agree on unpriced services. Every wording slip is gone. All rollups still reconcile with 0 difference over five date ranges, and 16 CSV streams came back unchanged. I score Pulse 92 against an estimated 52 for Easy Metrics, with every category at 8.5 or higher. It is clearly the better product and I would sign the purchase order. I am still not wowed, and the reasons are small but real. The by day share uses calendar days, so every work week shows a company margin above the job margin and the month to date number falls over a weekend. Month close shows 21.5% for November while Home shows 26.5%. A typed price can quietly override a warehouse contract rate while the page still credits the contract. The client guard misses plurals. Email is still deferred, and the database guard is off in production until someone sets a flag. I found no major problem this round.

blocking_issues.title: The guard readiness check can say ready when the app cannot use the plain role
blocking_issues.where: apps/pulse/drizzle/0009_db_guard_role.sql step 2, and dbGuardStatus in src/server/db/system.ts (GET /api/health)
blocking_issues.repro: On this PostgreSQL 16.15, as postgres: create role se_mig4 nosuperuser createrole; set session authorization se_mig4; create role se_app4 nologin noinherit. Then select pg_has_role(current_user,'se_app4','MEMBER') gives true, because the creator gets a membership with admin only (pg_auth_members shows admin_option t, set_option f). The step 2 test from the migration, 'if not pg_has_role(current_user, role, MEMBER) then grant', is skipped. Then 'begin; set local role se_app4' fails with 'permission denied to set role'. After an explicit 'grant se_app4 to se_mig4' the same SET ROLE works. The health check uses the same MEMBER test and never tries SET ROLE.
blocking_issues.why_it_matters: On PostgreSQL 16 or newer with a migration role that is not a superuser, which is the normal case on a hosted database, the migration passes, /api/health says guard ready true, and the moment PULSE_DB_GUARD=1 is set every guarded statement fails. The runbook tells the owner to trust ready true before turning the flag on. Fix: test for the SET right (pg_has_role with 'SET', or a real SET LOCAL ROLE in the health check) and always run the grant.

best_things: The database guard works in the running build. Queries run as pulse_app with the org set, the plain role cannot read auth tables or sibling schemas, cannot write another org, and my whole sweep left 0 refused statements in the server log.

The escape hatch is small and named. asSystem is used in 8 files, each with a reason, and a test fails when a new caller appears. I read every caller and found none that reads one org's pulse data for another.
The numbers still tie out to the cent for all 74 jobs in both orgs, across raw rows, v_facts, fact_days, job_stats and the API.
The part month company bridge is exact. 12 ranges in 2 orgs matched my own arithmetic, and the parts of a month always add back to the month.
The day save is now safe by design: one call, all or nothing, a version on every row, 409 with the fresh day, and one winner out of 10 parallel writers every time.
Money hiding held on 290 API URLs, 50 pages, 18 export streams and the zip for both no money roles, with the round three leak closed.
Sync is safe to run again and again: 0 new rows and 0 repeats after 6 runs, and the contract switch does what it says.
Tests are steady in both modes: 847 of 847 in 85 files with the guard on, and the same with it off.
The round four notes are honest about limits. Each limit I tested was exactly as written.
what_would_wow_me: Four things, all small next to what was built. First, make the guard the default: on in production, a login role that owns nothing so SET ROLE cannot be undone, a health check that really tries SET LOCAL ROLE, a grant that always runs, and one test through the transaction pooler. Second, fix the touch hit area on toasts so Undo works on a tablet, and add a touch test for it. Third, put the last guards in one place: the deleted job rule on every route that takes a job id, and the 'not after today' rule on extra services, materials and time not on a job. Fourth, a CI workflow that runs typecheck, lint and the 847 tests with the guard on. With the first two done I would sign the security review.
verdict_paragraph: Round four fixed five of my seven round three issues in full and the two biggest ones in their main part, and I proved each on the running system. The database guard is real: the app now runs its queries as a plain role with the workspace set, I watched it in pg_stat_activity, I could not get another org's rows as maya on any route, and the plain role cannot touch auth tables or sibling schemas. The day save went from the weakest write path to the strongest. Target margin no longer leaks, deleted jobs are closed on the named routes, future work dates are refused, the look alike guard is on every action, and contract rates have a switch and a fair 'from today' rule. The math is still exact, now with part month company costs too. I am not wowed yet for three reasons. The guard is off in production until someone sets a flag, and its readiness check gave a false green in my test with a non superuser role on PostgreSQL 16, which would turn that flag into an outage. The session still belongs to the table owner, so the guard stops honest bugs, not injected SQL. And Undo, the new safety net for saves and deletes, cannot be tapped on a touch screen. Pulse is a clearly better engineered product than Easy Metrics for a kitting shop, 88 against an estimated 52, and it is now close to what I would sign.

blocking_issues.title: Target pace by job shows no numbers on a phone
blocking_issues.where: /target-pace, 'Pace against target', By job, at 390 and 768, admin and supervisor
blocking_issues.repro: Sign in as j.okafor and open /target-pace at 390 by 844. Scroll to 'Pace against target'. The table is 760 px wide in a 340 px box. blocking_issues.where: /settings?section=catalogs Add a client, /jobs/<number>/work delete day confirm and Save the day, /services/<id> Set the price

blocking_issues.repro: Open /profit at 768 by 1024. Job is pinned at 304 px and Profit and Job margin at 116 px each. blocking_issues.title: Touch targets on a phone are too small in several places
blocking_issues.repro: At 390: /log/entries has 50 row checkboxes at 16 by 16 px. /alerts has row checkboxes at 14 by 14 px and 8 info buttons at 20 by 20 px. /settings/apps has 14 switches at 28 by 16 px, the new contract rate switch among them. blocking_issues.title: Settings on a phone hides 15 sections in one sideways strip

blocking_issues.title: The company profit sentence does not say why the company made more than its jobs
blocking_issues.where: /profit, the line under the cards, Nov 1 to Nov 19
blocking_issues.repro: Open /profit as admin. The line reads 'Your jobs made $132,009. After time not on a job and overhead, the company made $135,849. Company costs for 19 of 30 days.' blocking_issues.title: The focus ring and the error border are almost the same red
blocking_issues.where: Any form, for example the Log work 'Add a job' dialog
blocking_issues.repro: Open 'Add a job' on /log. The focused Client box has a border of rgb(200, 16, 46). Submit with a look alike name: the invalid border is rgb(179, 17, 44). Side by side they look the same. On the Work tab in dark mode a box that only has focus looks like a box with an error.

best_things: 350 of 350 page loads pass axe with 0 rules, with 0 console errors, 0 hydration warnings, 0 CSP reports and 0 pages wider than the screen, for both roles, both themes and three widths.
The day already has work state is the right design: it shows what the day holds before anything is saved, turns the main button off, and gives one button to open that day.
The delete day confirm lists what will go (500 good units, 5 scrapped, 52 labor hours, $1,392.84, Packer 48, Line lead 4) and says where to find it later. Undo works for delete, edit and clear.

Cards on a phone are well chosen: a job on Profit shows Revenue, Profit and Job margin, a client job shows Revenue, Cost, Profit, Margin and Units with its health chip, and an Entries day shows six numbers and two 40 px buttons.
Pinned Job, Cost, Profit and Job margin on the 18 column Job profit report, with a solid background in dark mode and a fade that stops beside the pinned columns.
One set of pickers. The labor class picker takes type ahead while closed ('m' gives Machine operator), opens with Enter, Space or Arrow down, and returns focus to itself on Enter and Escape.
The client box now behaves the same in the strip, the dialog and the wizard, with one message, a red border and focus in the box.
'No cost yet' and 'Not known' in place of a fake 100% margin, with a plain reason, and 'Set the price' right on the entry.
The contract rate switch strikes through its own promise line when it is off. That is a small touch that tells the truth.
The part month note names the days: '12 of 31 days in October and 10 of 30 days in November'.
Alert rules for a reader: says who can change them, shows On for each, and keeps money hidden.
The supervisor saw 0 dollar signs on 175 loads.
what_would_wow_me: I am close, and this is a one or two day list, not a redesign. One: put focus back on the button that opened the dialog after Add a client, the delete day confirm, Set the price, and after Save the day. Two: make 'Pace against target, By job' a card list under 768 like Profit, or pin Job and show Pace and Share of target first. Three: link 'Fix this first' and Home 'Open services' straight to the entries with no price. Four: do not print Profit $195 or Cost $0.00 for a service whose cost is not known. Five: get the Labeling service page under 0.1 at 390 so the count is 350 of 350. Six: in the already has work state, lock the boxes or hide them, and after a good save move the form on to a clean state. Seven: give phone checkboxes and switches a 24 px hit area at least, and 40 px on the floor screens. Eight: add a few words to the company profit line when the company made more than its jobs. Nine: make the error border differ from the focus ring by more than a shade. Do one through five and I sign.
verdict_paragraph: Round four fixed all ten of my round three blocking issues and all twelve of my PR 37 problems, and I saw each one work. The day form no longer overwrites a day, it shows what is there and sends you to edit it, with Undo on every write. Tables keep their money columns on screen or turn into cards, every scroll box has a name, a tab stop and a fade, no native picker is left, month close says one thing, and a service with no cost says so. My sweep of 350 loads came back with 0 axe rules and 0 console errors, and layout shift over 0.1 fell from 26 loads to 2. Pulse is far ahead of the Easy Metrics baseline, which I score from public evidence only, 52 against 92. I am not wowed yet, by a small margin, because fresh code left a short list of misses a designer would not sign: focus drops to the top of the page after four dialogs, the Target pace table shows no numbers on a phone, the red 'Fix this first' step links to a list with no filter, a service with unknown cost still prints a profit, and one page still jumps on a phone. None of these stops daily work and none is major. The database guard is on here and off in production until the owner flips it, and CI and email are deferred by the owner: I note those once and do not count them. Fix items one through five in my list and my answer becomes yes.
